links.outcome: Readability grade level of postoperative instructions after ChatGPT rewriting to target reading level
links.effect: Original instructions were 7th-8th grade; all fourth-grade-prompted rewrites reduced to sixth grade or below, but none reached fourth grade; only one sixth-grade-prompted rewrite reached sixth grade.
links.quote: Overall, the average readability of the original postoperative instructions ranged between the seventh and eighth grade levels.

links.outcome: Understandability, actionability, and safety of plain-language ChatGPT rewrites of patient instructions
links.effect: Understandability increased as reading levels decreased; actionability decreased for fourth-grade rewrites; safety not compromised in any rewrite.
links.quote: Understandability scores increased as reading levels decreased, whereas actionability scores decreased for fourth-grade rewrites.

screen.practice: reading-level constraint in prompts with surgeon safety review
screen.reason: The study empirically tests using LLM prompting constraints for specific reading levels (sixth vs. fourth grade) to simplify patient postoperative instructions and evaluates the resulting safety, understandability, and readability.
